seoTitle: How to Edit a Header in Elementor for Free in 2026
metaDescription: Think you need Elementor Pro to customize your header? Here's how to build a custom header and footer for free with a plugin, step by step from the WordPress admin.
intro: A common misconception among WordPress beginners is that editing a header requires Elementor Pro, but a free plugin that adds theme-builder functionality gets you the same result without paying for an upgrade. This guide follows the actual free-plugin route from inside the WordPress admin — finding the right plugin, opening its Header & Footer Builder, creating a template, and building the header itself inside Elementor's normal drag-and-drop editor. It works across popular themes like Astra, GeneratePress, OceanWP, and Hello Theme, since the plugin handles the header/footer logic independently of whichever theme you're running.

steps.heading: Confirm Elementor free doesn't include header editing
steps.body: Open the Elementor menu in your WordPress sidebar and you'll land on its home screen, with quick links to create a page or watch a guide, plus an AI chat box for generating a brief or sitemap. Nowhere on this screen is there a direct option to edit your site's header or footer — that theme-builder functionality is reserved for Elementor Pro in the base plugin, which is exactly why a separate free plugin is the workaround worth knowing about.

steps.heading: Install a free header and footer plugin
steps.body: In Plugins, search for and install a free theme-builder-style plugin — the one used here is Ultimate Addons for Elementor Lite, whose own description explains it plainly: it lets you create custom headers and footers with Elementor and display them in selected locations, plus build reusable Elementor blocks you can place anywhere with a shortcode. It shows up in your installed plugins list alongside whatever else is already active on the site.

image.caption: Ultimate Addons for Elementor Lite in the Plugins list — its own description confirms it adds custom header and footer creation without needing Elementor Pro.

steps.heading: Open the Header & Footer Builder
steps.body: Once activated, the plugin adds its own menu item to the WordPress sidebar with Dashboard, Header & Footer, Widgets, and Settings tabs. Click Header & Footer to reach the builder itself — on a fresh install this list is empty with an "Add New" button and no templates found, which is your starting point for building the header from scratch rather than editing an existing one.

image.caption: The plugin's Elementor Header & Footer Builder screen, empty and ready for a new template — reached from its own sidebar menu, separate from Elementor itself.

steps.heading: Create and name your header template
steps.body: Clicking Add New opens a standard WordPress edit screen where you name the template — something clear like "Main Header" makes it easy to find later if you build more than one. Saving and publishing here doesn't put anything live on your site yet; it just creates the template shell and generates a permalink for it, along with post-level controls like status, visibility, and a publish date, exactly like any other WordPress post type.

image.caption: A published header template named "PMN Main Header," with its own permalink and the usual WordPress Publish panel for status and visibility.

steps.heading: Build the header inside Elementor's editor
steps.body: From the template screen, the actual design work opens in Elementor's familiar drag-and-drop canvas, not a separate builder interface. You add widgets the same way you would on any page — an image placeholder for your logo, a text editor block for a tagline or heading, and additional widgets dropped into the empty zone below. This is the part that makes the free-plugin method work as well as Pro's built-in version: once you're inside the canvas, editing a header widget behaves identically to editing content on a normal page.

image.caption: The header template open in Elementor's standard editor, with an image placeholder and text block dropped in and an empty zone ready for more widgets.

steps.heading: Add navigation, logo, and sticky settings
steps.body: Swap the placeholder image for your real logo through Elementor's media library, and add a Nav Menu widget to pull in whichever WordPress menu you want displayed. Styling options in the widget's Style tab handle spacing, colors, and a sticky-header toggle so the header stays visible as visitors scroll, all without leaving the same editor you just used for the logo and text.

steps.heading: Set display rules and publish
steps.body: Back in the plugin's Header & Footer list, each template carries its own Display Rules column, which is what controls where the header actually appears — the whole site, specific pages, or particular post types. Set the rule to match your intent, publish the template, and it takes over your site's header immediately without touching your active theme's own header file, which is also why the same header survives a theme switch as long as the plugin stays active.

faq.question: Do I really need Elementor Pro to edit my header?
faq.answer: No — a free plugin like Ultimate Addons for Elementor Lite adds theme-builder functionality that lets you create and edit a custom header without upgrading to Elementor Pro.

faq.question: Does this method work with any WordPress theme?
faq.answer: It's compatible with popular themes including Astra, GeneratePress, OceanWP, and Hello Theme, since the header template runs through the plugin rather than the theme's own header file.

faq.question: Where do I find the Header & Footer Builder after installing the plugin?
faq.answer: The plugin adds its own menu item to the WordPress sidebar with a Header & Footer tab — that's separate from the main Elementor menu, so look there rather than inside Elementor itself.

faq.question: Why isn't my header showing or updating after I edit it?
faq.answer: Check the template's Display Rules first — if the rule doesn't match the page you're viewing, the header won't appear there even though it's published, which is a common cause of a header seeming stuck or missing.

faq.question: Can I add a sticky header using the free method?
faq.answer: Yes, sticky-header behavior is a styling option on the header widgets inside Elementor's editor, available once you've built the header through the free plugin.
